COMPONENT_SET.finding: The controlling record declares a required component this packet does not deliver, and no artifact in the family discloses the gap. KY.memo.json track ky_protective_order_record_expungement carries three components. components[0], role primary_filing, requirement 'required', AOC-275.18 — delivered, one page, correct. components[1], role court_order, requirement 'conditional', conditionDescription 'Reference only. The court enters the order.' — correctly not delivered. components[2], role service_instructions, requirement 'required', outputStrategy process_guidance, whose note reads in full: 'The Clerks' Manual directs that if the movant has not already served copies of the notice per the distribution list by first class mail, the clerk does. The packet tells the movant how to serve and provides the certificate.' The packet performs the first half — filing-instructions.md has a Service section that states the rule accurately. It does not perform the second: there is no certificate of service in this family. A case-insensitive search for the string 'certificate' across every file in the family directory returns nothing. The record's manualCompletionItems[1] compounds it by locating a manual step 'whereInPacket: Notice distribution list', a component the packet does not contain under that or any other name. Meanwhile product-wiring.json binding.instrumentKinds and MASTER_QUEUE.json both advertise instrumentKinds ['court_order','primary_filing','service_instructions'] while packetComponents lists only the primary filing and build-status.json records builtDocuments 1. build-findings.json reports blocking [] and findingCount 0 and does not mention the absent certificate at all, so a reader of the build artifacts has no way to learn of it. FIX06 recorded 'No certificate of service was authored' under what it deliberately did not do, which records the repair lane's scope but is not a disclosure inside the packet and does not reach the participant or the reviewer.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: The respondent-name repair is sound, and that part re-passes: the three respondent widgets carry the participant's decomposed name in both fixtures, at their own rectangles, left to right in first/middle/last order by x-position, and the PETITIONER block carries zero participant ink in both. The failure is elsewhere and is on the delivered boundary page. The boundary fixture writes the 'movant' anchor from participant.full_legal_name with the value 'Alexandrina-Katharine Montgomery-Vandenberg-Oyelaran', while the same page's caption names the respondent 'Alexandrina-Katharine | Montgomery-Vandenberg-Oyelaran | Fitzwilliam III'. On this form the movant and the respondent are the same person — the form's own sentence is 'The movant, ____, seeks expungement of the records of this case' directly above that caption — and the delivered page names that person two different ways, dropping the surname and generational suffix from the operative sentence. Read at the source: BOUNDARY sets participant.last_name to 'Fitzwilliam III' but sets participant.full_legal_name to a string that omits it, so the composed identity contradicts its own parts. The canonical fixture does not have this problem: 'Jordan Avery Reyes' is exactly first plus middle plus last. This is a source-authored default that reaches the page, and it survives every counter: the map declares the anchor, the finalizer wrote what the map's fact held, the ink lands inside the write box, and nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes stays 0. It has a second consequence recorded under CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP: because the shortened value fits, the movant field's overflow behaviour was never exercised at the width the fixture's own persona implies.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: Nothing was written into a field or region this form reserves to the court or the clerk. 'Court' and 'Division' are withheld with approvedDisposition REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and carry no ink in either fixture. The NOTIFICATION OF EXPUNGEMENT HEARING block — the hearing date, the hour, the a.m./p.m. election, the District/Circuit election and the clerk's dated signature — carries no AcroForm widget at all on this form, and per-token attribution over both delivered files found no added ink anywhere below y=545.86. The Print and Reset push buttons were suppressed before the flatten and neither caption appears in either delivered file.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: Measured on the delivered bytes rather than on intent, and clean. Every added word token in both fixtures fits wholly inside exactly one source widget rectangle at a 2pt tolerance; none matched two rectangles and none matched none. The tightest case is boundary 'middle res', where 'Montgomery-Vandenberg-Oyelaran' ends at x 338.06 inside a rectangle whose right edge is 344.72, with the neighbouring 'last res' rectangle beginning at 345.25 — no collision. The builder shrinks to fit rather than clipping: that token renders 7.86pt tall against canonical's 10.17pt. Where a value cannot be made to fit it is refused rather than clipped, and the refusal is recorded with the measured widget width: boundary's 36-character case number is refused against a 111.16pt widget and reports/blanks.json states why. That is the right behaviour for a filing. Recorded against this obligation without changing its result: the boundary fixture does not actually exercise the 'movant' anchor at its own persona's full width, because its participant.full_legal_name omits the surname the same persona carries (see KNOWN_PREFILLS). The full composed name would run roughly 380pt against a 315.36pt widget and would therefore have hit the refusal path, leaving the form's operative sentence 'The movant, ____, seeks expungement' blank on a filing. Whether that path is the right one for this field is untested here because the fixture never reaches it.

evidence.boundaryCoverageGap: the movant anchor at true persona width

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Counted, not accepted. The record's legalDesignDecision.limitations holds 4 entries: 2 classified packet_instruction, 1 classified participant_question and 1 classified self_help_boundary. Its selfHelpStopConditions holds 4. Every one of the 2 packet_instruction limitations, the 1 self_help_boundary and the 4 selfHelpStopConditions — 7 statements — reaches participant-instructions.md by exact string containment, tested programmatically against the live record nodes, and each is labelled there as the record's own words. That includes the one that matters most on this route: 'This clears the civil protective-order case record only. It does not touch any criminal record arising from the same events.' The fourth limitation is classified participant_question rather than an instruction or a boundary and is not claimed to reach the guide; its substance — that the two gates must be asked — surfaces as the three disclosed sworn allegations. None of the record's prose is printed onto the filing itself; all 54 and 128 added glyphs are persona facts, so the internal-record-text-printed-on-a-filing defect is absent.

evidence.method: literal string containment of each live record node against the delivered participant-instructions.md

SERVICE.finding: The service rule the packet states is accurate to the record. rules.service reads 'The movant may serve copies of the notice by first class mail per the distribution list; otherwise the clerk does', and filing-instructions.md states exactly that. The copies list it gives — the court file, the petitioner and the respondent — matches the form's own printed footer, which this lane read in the source's text layer. No service deadline is asserted, and the record states none. Two things are recorded here without changing the result. First, the sentence is a hardcoded literal, not a read of rules.service, which is the residual condition described under crossChecks. Second, the missing certificate of service is a service-related defect but it is a missing component and is scored once, under COMPONENT_SET, rather than counted twice; a repair lane should read the two together.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: Everything the participant or the clerk must complete is enumerated, in the right place, with a reason. Five AcroForm fields carry approvedDisposition REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING — Division, Court, and the three petitioner-name fields — each with a whatToSupply string, and all five reappear in participant-instructions.md under 'You must supply these before you file'. The three numbered checkboxes are classified PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE and each carries a reason explaining that it is a sworn allegation above the participant's signature; the guide states plainly that the packet checks none of them. The four printed lines with no widget behind them — Date, Signature, Address and Telephone Number of Movant, and the NOTIFICATION OF EXPUNGEMENT HEARING block — are enumerated with the party responsible for each. The petitioner-name entries no longer rest on a claimed silence: they explain that the record places the participant in the respondent block and that the petitioner block names a third person the platform does not hold.

ARTIFACTS.finding: The artifact set is complete and bound to the right bytes. Both fixture digests were recomputed twice here, with sha256sum and with node crypto, and agree with reports/rendered-artifacts.json and with the digests carried in product-wiring.json. Byte lengths and page counts agree. The two output-byte glyph readings are present on both artifacts and both reproduce independently: 54 added non-whitespace glyph characters in canonical and 128 in boundary, matching my own diff of the delivered text against the pinned source exactly. This family does not join the twenty-five overlay directories that emit neither. One inaccuracy is recorded without failing the obligation, because it does not change the page and the headline figures are right: in reports/actual-writes.json the per-write field textReadFromFinalPdfBytes reports 'JordanA' (7 glyphs) for 'first res' and 'AveryR' (6) for 'middle res' in canonical, and 'Alexandrina-KatharineM' (22) and 'Montgomery-Vandenberg-OyelaranF' (31) in boundary. The delivered files contain no such strings. The cause is the ±2pt horizontal tolerance in the per-write readback: 'first res' ends at x 203.00 and 'middle res' begins at x 203.38, so the neighbour's first glyph falls inside the tolerance. The report's own per-write counts consequently sum to 56 against a stated document total of 54. This matters more than a typo because that same tolerance is the machinery that would have to distinguish a name landing in an adjacent caption block, which is the defect class this family was repaired for.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: Measured against the widget's own option list, read from the source bytes, which is the cross-check this obligation exists for. Case.County is the form's only option-bearing field; its /Opt array holds 121 entries, each a two-element [exportValue, displayValue] pair. The delivered canonical county 'Franklin' is the display value at index 37 and the delivered boundary county 'Breckinridge' is the display value at index 14, so both delivered values are members of the widget's own list and neither is invented. No option the route requires is absent. Recorded without changing the result: the builder's own evidence for this is empty rather than affirmative. reports/actual-writes.json publishes deliveredChoiceValues [] and choiceValuesOutsideTheirOwnOptions [] for both fixtures, but that check runs against the DELIVERED bytes after flattening, where no AcroForm and no dropdown survive, so the loop never executes and both arrays are empty by construction rather than by measurement. Read as a test for choice state surviving the flatten it is meaningful and correctly empty; read as evidence that the delivered county is on its own option list — which is how FIX06's cross-check note uses it — it carries nothing. This obligation passes on the measurement recorded here, not on that zero.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: Measured and does not arise, which is a measurement rather than an absence. AOC-275.18 is a one-page motion carrying 16 discrete AcroForm fields, enumerated here from the source bytes: two push buttons, a case number, a county chooser, a court and a division, six caption name fields in two fixed rows of three, a movant line and three checkboxes. There is no charge table, no count table, no indexed row family and no repeating structure of any kind, so no row can be incomplete and no AcroForm index can disagree with a printed row number. The related trap was nevertheless tested where it could bite: the two three-field caption rows were resolved by geometry against the form's printed captions rather than by their field names, and the left-to-right order within the written row was confirmed by x-position — first res at x 38.30, middle res at 203.38, last res at 345.25 — against the record's first/middle/last facts.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: filing-instructions.md tells the participant, under 'The filing fee': 'The committed record says the Clerks' Manual records no filing fee for this motion. It does not record a fee-waiver treatment, and this packet states no fee amount. Ask the clerk.' The first clause is accurate — rules.fees reads 'none identified. The Clerks' Manual records no filing fee for this motion.' The second is false. The record does record a fee-waiver treatment: rules.feeWaiver exists and reads 'not applicable; no fee is identified.' And the builder never opens it. loadControllingRecord() captures fees, service, notarization and participantSignature from the rules node and does not capture feeWaiver, so nothing in the build reaches that field. This is the same defect the family was just repaired for, surviving in the sibling document: a negative claim about what a record does not say, unfalsifiable from inside the packet, asserted by a builder that does not read the node it is describing, and wrong. It is worse than a stale paraphrase because it cannot go stale loudly — no assertion guards it. The wider condition is that filing-instructions.md is built entirely from hardcoded string literals: every one of its 'The committed record says...' sentences is a lines.push() literal, and RECORD.fees, RECORD.service, RECORD.notarization, RECORD.participantSignature and RECORD.clerkDuties are all loaded by the repaired loader and none of them is used to build this document. FIX06 recorded that it left filing-instructions.md alone and that its prose 'is still a paraphrase rather than a read'; on the fee-waiver sentence that paraphrase is not merely unread, it contradicts the record. Recorded alongside, and part of the same literal block: 'The record does not state a service deadline or a filing deadline, so this packet states none.' No deadline node exists under rules, so as to deadlines that is true, but the record does carry a timing rule at waitingPeriods — condition 'Dismissal of the protective-order petition without a full order having issued', duration 'six months from the dismissal' — which is the whole gate of this route and which the builder also never reads.
